advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make _proxy_refusal_of recurse into legs that are themselves exception groups, so a nested all-refused group counts as a proxy refusal
evidence: src/rebar/llm/failure.py:248: texts = [_proxy_refusal(leg) for leg in legs]

No test in tests/unit/test_llm_proxy_refusal.py builds a nested group
advisory.finding: _proxy_refusal_of does not look inside nested exception groups. A FallbackExceptionGroup that contains another FallbackExceptionGroup, where every leg is a proxy refusal, is classified CHANGE_PROVIDER_OR_MODEL with no proxy_refused error_type. The inner group on its own is classified CHANGE_SETTINGS. _classify_fallback_group recurses into legs through classify_llm_failure, but _proxy_refusal_of calls _proxy_refusal(leg), and that only walks __cause__/__context__, never .exceptions.
scenarios: A FallbackModel used as a leg of another FallbackModel behind a sandbox egress proxy that refuses every provider host
advisory.suggested_fix: In _proxy_refusal_of, build texts with `[_proxy_refusal_of(leg) for leg in legs]` (recursive) instead of `_proxy_refusal(leg)`, and add a nested-group test.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Only treat an outcome as a proxy refusal (in the diagnostic and in close_gate_remedy) when its resolution class is CHANGE_SETTINGS, so class and error_type cannot disagree
evidence: src/rebar/llm/failure.py:200-203: refusal = _proxy_refusal_of(exc) / if refusal is not None: diag["error_type"] = PROXY_REFUSED  (runs after the ModelHTTPError body error_type is set)
src/rebar/llm/failure.py:761: if outcome is not None and (outcome.diagnostic or {}).get("error_type") == PROXY_REFUSED: return PROXY_REFUSED_REMEDY
message_for gates on both: `if error_type == PROXY_REFUSED and resolution_class == ResolutionClass.CHANGE_SETTINGS.value`
src/rebar/llm/failure.py:334-356: earlier _map arms return before _map_tail's proxy check runs
advisory.finding: close_gate_remedy returns PROXY_REFUSED_REMEDY whenever diagnostic error_type == 'proxy_refused', without checking that the outcome is CHANGE_SETTINGS. message_for does check the class. _base_diagnostic sets that error_type whenever the cause/context chain holds a 4xx ProxyError. It does this separately from _map, whose earlier arms (ConnectError, timeouts, ModelHTTPError, UsageLimitExceeded, ...) can return another class for the same exception. It also overwrites a ModelHTTPError's error_type taken from the response body.
scenarios: A timeout or other typed error whose implicit __context__ is an earlier handled 4xx ProxyError: the class is WAIT_AND_RETRY, but the close gate prints the proxy remedy
advisory.suggested_fix: In close_gate_remedy, also require `outcome.resolution_class is ResolutionClass.CHANGE_SETTINGS` before returning PROXY_REFUSED_REMEDY.

The function's unchanged docstring still says every group whose legs are all non-retryable keeps CHANGE_PROVIDER_OR_MODEL. That is now false for a group in which every leg is a proxy refusal.

tests/unit/test_llm_proxy_refusal.py: every `_group(...)` call takes `_proxy_leg()` or ModelHTTPError legs; no group is ever passed a group as a leg
advisory.finding: No test covers a nested fallback group, and the new group-refusal logic gets it wrong. Example input: `_group(_group(_proxy_leg(), _proxy_leg()), _proxy_leg())`. The inner group classifies CHANGE_SETTINGS and the plain leg also classifies CHANGE_SETTINGS. But the outer group falls through to CHANGE_PROVIDER_OR_MODEL with no `proxy_refused` error_type. The cause is that `_proxy_refusal_of(outer)` calls `_proxy_refusal(inner_group)`, which only walks the inner group's own `__cause__`/`__context__` chain and never looks at its `.exceptions`. So the inner group reads as not refused, and `all(texts)` is False.
scenarios: A FallbackModel whose candidates include another FallbackModel, all behind a refusing egress proxy: the outer verdict says 'switch model/provider' instead of naming the proxy, and the proxy remedy and message are skipped
advisory.suggested_fix: In `_proxy_refusal_of`, use `texts = [_proxy_refusal_of(leg) for leg in legs]` so nested groups recurse, and add the nested-group test above.

src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:129-131: `if coverage.get("retryable"): return 11` / `return indeterminate_code if verdict == "INDETERMINATE" else 1`
advisory.finding: `test_degraded_verdict_prints_the_proxy_refusal` checks only `!= 11`. The expected result is exactly 2: the verdict is INDETERMINATE, the outcome is not retryable, and `indeterminate_code=2`. A regression that returned 1, or 0, would still pass.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Limit the proxy-refusal regex to policy statuses (e.g. 403/407, or 4xx excluding 408/429) so transient 408/429 proxy answers keep RETRY_NOW/WAIT_AND_RETRY
evidence: src/rebar/llm/failure.py:220: `_PROXY_REFUSAL_STATUS = re.compile(r"\s*4\d\d\b")` matches any 4xx, including 408 and 429
src/rebar/llm/failure.py:235: `if isinstance(node, httpx.ProxyError) and _PROXY_REFUSAL_STATUS.match(str(node)):`, so a ProxyError("429 Too Many Requests") counts as a refusal
Primary failure: ModelAPIError <- APIConnectionError <- httpx.ProxyError("429 ...") from a throttling egress proxy
Old surfaced disposition: the ModelAPIError arm returned RETRY_NOW (failure.py:366-367 before the new check), so retryable=True per _RETRYABLE (failure.py:40-42, 384)

New surfaced disposition: failure.py:364-365 `if _proxy_refusal(exc) is not None: return ResolutionClass.CHANGE_SETTINGS`, so retryable=False; for a group whose every leg hit the same throttling proxy, failure.py:302-305 also returns CHANGE_SETTINGS instead of RETRY_NOW

Callers that change behavior: src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:95 `return 11 if getattr(o, "retryable", False) else 1` and src/rebar/_commands/completion_verifier_run.py:41 `returncode = 11 if (outcome and outcome.retryable) else 1` now exit 1 (fail-closed) instead of 11 (transient, retry)

Messaging also becomes wrong: message_for returns PROXY_REFUSED_MESSAGE ("a fixed proxy policy ... an immediate retry cannot succeed"), and close_gate_remedy returns PROXY_REFUSED_REMEDY, telling the operator to change the proxy allowlist for a temporary throttle
Even the module's own reasoning (failure.py:213-218) calls only policy refusals (403 allowlist, 407) unretryable; neither the tests nor the docs cover 408 or 429
advisory.finding: _PROXY_REFUSAL_STATUS matches any 4xx answer to CONNECT, not just policy refusals. A proxy that answers CONNECT with a transient 429 Too Many Requests (rate limiting) or 408 Request Timeout is now classified CHANGE_SETTINGS (non-retryable) instead of RETRY_NOW (retryable). Gate callers that used to exit 11 and retry now exit 1 and give up.
scenarios: A corporate or sandbox egress proxy rate-limits CONNECT with `429 Too Many Requests` during a burst of gate calls. Before: RETRY_NOW, exit 11, the orchestrator retries and succeeds. After: CHANGE_SETTINGS, exit 1, the gate fails closed and tells the operator to edit the proxy allowlist.
A proxy answers `408 Request Timeout` to a slow CONNECT and gets classified as a permanent setting problem.
advisory.suggested_fix: Narrow `_PROXY_REFUSAL_STATUS` so it skips 408 and 429, e.g. `re.compile(r"\s*4(?!08\b|29\b)\d\d\b")`, or allow only the policy statuses (`r"\s*(?:403|407)\b"`). Optionally map a proxy 429 to WAIT_AND_RETRY. Add tests showing that ProxyError("429 Too Many Requests") and ProxyError("408 Request Timeout") stay retryable.
